basic_information.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
basic_information.creator: OpenAI
basic_information.release_date: April 16, 2025 (open-source CLI release); May 2025 (Codex cloud preview in ChatGPT)
basic_information.license: Apache 2.0 (open-source CLI); proprietary (cloud service and underlying models)

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: single_agent, code_first. Codex CLI is a lightweight terminal-based coding agent that follows a read-plan-execute loop: it reads the codebase, plans changes, edits files, and runs commands inside an OS-enforced sandbox. It can also operate as an MCP server for multi-agent orchestration via the OpenAI Agents SDK.
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Codex-specific model family: (1) codex-1 — based on o3, optimized for software engineering via reinforcement learning on real coding tasks (May 2025); (2) codex-mini-latest — fine-tuned o4-mini for CLI use ($1.50/1M input, $6/1M output tokens, 75% caching discount); (3) GPT-5-Codex — purpose-built for Codex CLI (September 2025); (4) GPT-5.1-Codex and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max (November 2025); (5) GPT-5.2-Codex — state-of-the-art on SWE-Bench Pro 56.4% and Terminal-Bench 2.0 64.0% (January 14, 2026); (6) GPT-5.3-Codex — 25% faster, tops SWE-Bench Pro and Terminal-Bench 2.0 (February 5, 2026). Users can switch models at runtime via /model slash command.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: Built-in tools: shell command execution (sandboxed), file read/write, web search (enabled by default with search cache). External tools via MCP: Codex supports MCP server configuration in ~/.codex/config.toml, launches STDIO or streaming HTTP MCP servers automatically at session start, and exposes their tools alongside built-ins. Codex itself can run as an MCP server (codex() and codex-reply() tools) for orchestration by the OpenAI Agents SDK.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: code_as_plan. Codex reads the repository, generates a plan for changes, then executes edits and shell commands iteratively. It uses reinforcement learning-trained models that generate code mirroring human style and PR preferences, run tests iteratively until passing. The agent follows a conversational loop where it proposes actions, receives approval (in suggest/auto-edit modes), and executes them.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: Not built-in as a first-class feature, but supported via MCP server mode + OpenAI Agents SDK orchestration. When exposed as an MCP server, multiple Codex instances can be orchestrated by an Agents SDK supervisor, enabling multi-agent workflows (e.g., one agent writes code, another reviews, another tests). The Agents SDK handles hand-offs and tracing across agents.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term (conversation within session), episodic (session transcripts stored locally for resume), semantic (AGENTS.md project instructions loaded at session start), procedural (none explicit). Codex stores transcripts locally so users can resume previous sessions with full context.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Auto-compaction: SessionState tracks token usage and triggers automatic context compaction when approaching the context window limit, replacing verbose history with concise summaries. This enables significantly longer effective sessions without hitting context limits or degraded performance. The codex resume command reopens earlier threads preserving the original transcript, plan history, and approvals.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: file_system. Session transcripts (rollout files) are persisted locally on disk. SQLite-backed log database introduced in recent versions for improved session management with thread-id filtering, retention policies, and heuristic coloring. Configuration stored in ~/.codex/config.toml.
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Context is a first-class concern: (1) AGENTS.md layered instruction system — global (~/.codex/AGENTS.md) + project-level (walked from root to CWD), with override files and configurable fallback filenames, capped at 32 KiB combined; (2) auto-compaction prevents context overflow; (3) session resume reconstructs conversation history by replaying rollout items; (4) MCP tool descriptions are injected into context alongside built-in tools.

capabilities.core_capabilities: Full-screen terminal UI (TUI) for interactive coding sessions. Can read, change, and run code in the working directory. Key capabilities include: (1) Feature development — write new features from natural language descriptions; (2) Bug fixing — diagnose and fix bugs with codebase context; (3) Code refactoring — large refactors, migrations, and codebase modernization; (4) Test writing and execution — generate tests and run them iteratively until passing; (5) Pull request generation — propose PRs for review; (6) Codebase Q&A — answer questions about code; (7) Multimodal input — accepts text, screenshots, and diagrams to generate/edit code; (8) Web search — built-in first-party web search tool enabled by default; (9) Session resume — pick up previous sessions with full context; (10) File search — tracks CWD changes, supports multi-root traversal; (11) Steer mode — Enter sends immediately during running tasks, Tab queues follow-up input; (12) Slash commands — /model to switch models, /compact for manual compaction, etc. Cloud Codex additionally supports: parallel task execution, GitHub integration for automated PRs, and Automations for unprompted routine work (issue triage, alert monitoring, CI/CD).
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text, code, vision (screenshots/diagrams as input), file system (read/write/execute), shell commands, web search
capabilities.autonomy_level: Configurable across three modes: (1) suggest — safest, requires approval for all actions (copilot); (2) auto-edit — approves file edits automatically, confirms shell commands (human_in_loop); (3) full-auto — executes everything autonomously within sandbox constraints (fully_autonomous within sandbox). Also has dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox for externally hardened environments.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: Built-in: shell execution, file operations, web search. Extensible via MCP: any MCP-compatible server can be added (STDIO or streaming HTTP). Configuration via CLI (codex mcp commands) or config.toml. Can connect to the broader MCP ecosystem of tools. Also integrates with the OpenAI Agents SDK for multi-agent orchestration.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Full MCP support, both as client and server. As client: connects to MCP servers configured in config.toml, launches them at session start. As server: exposes codex() and codex-reply() tools for orchestration by external agents. Managed via codex mcp CLI commands.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: No direct A2A (Agent-to-Agent Protocol by Google) support documented. Inter-agent communication is handled through MCP server mode + OpenAI Agents SDK orchestration rather than the A2A protocol.
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: Full AGENTS.md support. Codex reads AGENTS.md files before doing any work. Discovery and precedence: global scope (~/.codex/ — reads AGENTS.override.md if exists, else AGENTS.md), then project scope (walks from project root to CWD). Supports override files, configurable fallback filenames via project_doc_fallback_filenames in config.toml, and a 32 KiB combined size limit (project_doc_max_bytes).
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: High interoperability: (1) MCP client/server for tool ecosystem compatibility; (2) OpenAI Agents SDK integration for multi-agent orchestration; (3) Available as a GitHub agent (February 2026) alongside Claude on GitHub Agent HQ for Copilot Pro+ and Enterprise customers; (4) VS Code extension available; (5) Open-source CLI can be embedded in custom workflows. However, tightly coupled to OpenAI's model ecosystem — cannot use non-OpenAI models.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: Layered sandbox + approval policy: Sandbox modes: (1) read-only (default) — agent can only read files; (2) workspace-write — can write within active workspace, no network by default; (3) danger-full-access — no sandbox restrictions (extremely risky). OS-level enforcement: macOS uses Seatbelt policies, Linux uses Landlock + seccomp. Network access disabled by default, configurable opt-in. Write permissions limited to active workspace by default.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Approval policies control when agent pauses for human confirmation: (1) 'untrusted' — requires approval for all actions; (2) 'on-request' — auto-approves most actions, asks for potentially dangerous ones; (3) 'on-failure' — only asks when something fails; (4) 'never' — fully autonomous (only with sandbox protection). In auto-edit mode, Codex asks approval for commands but auto-approves file edits. In full-auto mode, it still asks for actions outside workspace or requiring network.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Reinforcement learning training on real-world coding tasks ensures code mirrors human style and passes tests. Iterative test execution — agent runs tests until passing, catching incorrect outputs. Sandbox isolation prevents hallucinated commands from causing damage. Code review workflow (suggest mode) lets humans verify all changes before execution.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Comprehensive tracing: Codex automatically records traces capturing every prompt, tool call, and hand-off. Traces dashboard shows execution timeline, MCP calls, files written, execution durations. SQLite-backed log database for local session logging. OpenTelemetry integration available for external monitoring (SigNoz, Datadog).
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: Configurable: (1) pre-approval (suggest mode — all actions require human OK); (2) selective pre-approval (auto-edit mode — commands need approval, edits are auto-approved); (3) confidence_threshold equivalent (full-auto mode — only asks for out-of-scope actions like network access or writes outside workspace); (4) always_on (suggest mode default for safety). Users choose their comfort level at CLI startup or via configuration.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: OpenAI. The CLI is open-source under Apache 2.0 on GitHub (openai/codex). OpenAI maintains the project, accepts community contributions, and controls the underlying model releases.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: Implements and promotes: (1) Model Context Protocol (MCP) — both client and server; (2) AGENTS.md convention for project instructions; (3) OpenAI Agents SDK protocol for multi-agent orchestration; (4) OpenTelemetry for observability traces. 285 contributors on GitHub as of early 2026.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: Inherits OpenAI's enterprise compliance: SOC 2 Type 2 (Security and Confidentiality) for ChatGPT business products and API. OpenAI has committed to EU AI Act compliance and signed the EU Code of Practice. Data residency options available for enterprise customers (US, Europe, UK, Japan, Canada, South Korea, Singapore, Australia, India, UAE). Local CLI mode keeps code on user's machine — beneficial for privacy-sensitive workflows.

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: local (CLI runs on user's machine — macOS, Linux, Windows), cloud (Codex cloud runs in OpenAI-managed isolated containers via ChatGPT), hybrid (CLI with API key for model access + local execution). Also available as GitHub integration and VS Code extension.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: Local CLI: single-user, single-task. Cloud Codex: can run multiple tasks in parallel in isolated containers. For scaling: expose CLI as MCP server and orchestrate multiple instances via Agents SDK for multi-agent pipelines. Serverless model access via API.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: CLI access included with ChatGPT subscriptions: Plus ($20/month), Pro ($200/month), Business ($25/user/month), Enterprise (custom pricing). API pay-as-you-go: codex-mini-latest at $1.50/1M input tokens, $6/1M output tokens (75% prompt caching discount). Cost per task varies by complexity — simple tasks may cost $0.01-0.10, complex multi-file refactors significantly more. Most developers find subscription better value than per-API-call pricing.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: CLI: macOS, Windows, or Linux machine with terminal. Originally required Node.js v22+ (npm install), now available as standalone Rust binary via brew install --cask codex. Minimal local compute — heavy computation happens on OpenAI's servers. Requires internet connection for API calls to OpenAI models. Cloud Codex: no local requirements beyond a web browser (runs in ChatGPT).

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: Built-in: OpenAI Traces dashboard for inspecting execution timelines, prompts, tool calls, hand-offs, and durations. External: OpenTelemetry support (BatchTraceProcessor + BackendSpanExporter), SigNoz integration documented, Datadog integration available. Custom trace processors can be added via add_trace_processor() for additional processing alongside OpenAI backend traces.
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes — comprehensive built-in tracing. Every prompt, tool call, hand-off, file write, and execution duration is automatically recorded. Traces can be viewed in the OpenAI Traces dashboard or exported via OpenTelemetry. SQLite-backed local log database with thread-id filtering introduced in recent versions.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: production_ready. Actively used by OpenAI's own engineering teams (Security, Product Engineering, Frontend, API, Infrastructure, Performance). Adopted by enterprises including Cisco, Temporal, and Superhuman. 327 releases, regular updates (latest rust-v0.98.0), mature sandbox and security model. Available on GitHub Agent HQ for enterprise customers.

adoption_and_market.github_stars: 59,600+ stars, 7,800+ forks on GitHub (openai/codex) as of early 2026
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: Included with all ChatGPT paid plans (Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, Enterprise) — millions of potential users. 327 releases and 285 contributors. Used internally across OpenAI engineering teams. Enterprise customers include Cisco, Temporal, Superhuman. Available on GitHub Agent HQ for Copilot Pro+ and Enterprise customers (February 2026). Exact active user count not publicly disclosed.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: Freemium + pay-as-you-go. CLI is free and open-source (Apache 2.0). Model access via ChatGPT subscription (Plus $20/mo, Pro $200/mo, Business $25/user/mo, Enterprise custom) or API key with per-token billing. Cloud Codex included in ChatGPT subscriptions with credit-based usage limits.
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: Primary: (1) Feature development from natural language; (2) Bug diagnosis and fixing; (3) Large-scale code refactoring and migrations; (4) Test generation and execution; (5) Pull request creation and review; (6) Codebase understanding and Q&A; (7) Repetitive task automation (test coverage improvement, integration fixes); (8) CI/CD automation via Codex Automations. Industries: software development, DevOps, enterprise engineering, startups. Used by Temporal for feature development and debugging, Superhuman for test coverage and integration fixes, Cisco for engineering acceleration.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: Direct competitors: Anthropic Claude Code (terminal agent, strong at complex reasoning and test-driven development), GitHub Copilot (IDE-integrated, inline suggestions), Cursor (AI-native IDE), Devin by Cognition (fully autonomous agent). Strengths vs competitors: (1) OpenAI model ecosystem with rapidly improving Codex-specific models; (2) OS-level sandbox security (Seatbelt/Landlock) unique among terminal agents; (3) Both local CLI and cloud modes; (4) Open-source CLI under Apache 2.0; (5) Deep GitHub integration. Weaknesses: tightly coupled to OpenAI models only, relatively newer than some competitors in the terminal agent space.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: Configurable across the full spectrum: copilot (suggest mode — proposes changes, human approves everything) | assistant (auto-edit mode — executes file edits autonomously, asks for shell commands) | autonomous (full-auto mode — acts independently within sandbox constraints). Default is suggest mode (safest). User chooses at startup or via config.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Approval-based handoff: agent pauses execution and presents proposed actions in the TUI for human review. In suggest mode, every action is a handoff point. In auto-edit mode, shell commands trigger handoff. In full-auto mode, only out-of-scope actions (network, external writes) trigger handoff. The conversational TUI allows real-time steering — users can provide follow-up instructions, adjust direction, or abort. Steer mode (stable since v0.98.0) lets Enter send immediately during running tasks.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Session-level: users provide real-time feedback via the conversational TUI, agent adjusts within the session. Project-level: AGENTS.md files encode persistent preferences and instructions that shape all future sessions. Model-level: OpenAI's Codex models are trained via reinforcement learning on real-world coding tasks, incorporating patterns from accepted PRs and human preferences. No explicit user feedback mechanism that improves the model per-user (no personalized fine-tuning).

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Highly relevant for startup founders and small engineering teams. When to use: (1) Small teams needing to move fast — Codex handles repetitive tasks (tests, migrations, refactoring) so developers focus on architecture and product; (2) Solo founders who need a 'coding partner' for feature development and debugging; (3) Startups already in the OpenAI ecosystem (using GPT models) — natural fit with existing API keys; (4) Teams wanting open-source tooling they can customize (Apache 2.0 CLI). When to avoid: (1) If your codebase contains highly sensitive IP and you cannot use cloud APIs — though local CLI mode mitigates this; (2) If your stack requires non-OpenAI models (Codex is locked to OpenAI); (3) If you need deep IDE integration over terminal workflows — consider Cursor or Copilot instead; (4) Very early-stage exploration where simpler tools (ChatGPT web, Copilot inline) suffice.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: Buy (subscribe) in almost all cases. The CLI is free and open-source, model access costs $20-200/month via ChatGPT plans or per-token via API. Building your own coding agent from scratch would cost months of engineering time. Cost-benefit: a ChatGPT Plus subscription ($20/month) gives access to Codex CLI + cloud Codex — exceptional value if it saves even a few hours/month of developer time. For startups building developer tools, the open-source CLI can be embedded or extended under Apache 2.0. For most startups, Codex is a tool to use, not a component to rebuild.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (AI project management — understanding agentic coding tools for team productivity), Session 5 (ethics and governance — sandbox security model, enterprise compliance). Also relevant to Session 2 (hands-on tools demonstration) and Session 4 (business models — OpenAI's pricing strategy, developer tools market).

confidence.data_quality: High. Based on official OpenAI documentation (developers.openai.com), official blog posts (openai.com/index/), GitHub repository (openai/codex), and reputable third-party sources. Model timeline confirmed across multiple official announcements.
confidence.cross_reference: Official sources: OpenAI blog, developers.openai.com documentation, GitHub repository, OpenAI Help Center. Third-party confirmation: DevOps.com, InfoWorld, Sequoia Capital, DeepLearning.AI, SmartScope, DataCamp, Builder.io, Graphite. GitHub metrics independently verifiable.
confidence.caveats: Rapidly evolving product — new model versions released monthly (GPT-5.3-Codex is days old as of February 2026). Rust rewrite is relatively recent; some features may still be stabilizing. GitHub stars and contributor counts are approximate snapshots. Codex CLI is locked to OpenAI models — no provider flexibility. Cloud Codex usage limits tied to ChatGPT subscription tier. The 'Codex' name was previously used for OpenAI's 2021 code completion model (descendant of GPT-3) — this is an entirely different product. Pricing and model availability may change rapidly.
